questions.prompt: You correct the agent — "our API tests need a local Redis" — and it saves a note. Next week you start a fresh session and the agent already knows. Which file carried that knowledge?
options: A topic file in the auto memory directory, indexed by `MEMORY.md`
The session transcript from last week, which is replayed at startup
The system prompt, which now includes your correction
questions.explanation: Claude writes auto memory itself, as topic files indexed by MEMORY.md. Option 2 is tempting because transcripts are stored on disk — but the next session does not replay them; only the memory files load.

questions.prompt: `MEMORY.md` has grown to 400 lines. What does the next session actually load?
options: All 400 lines, because MEMORY.md is loaded in full
The first 200 lines or 25KB, whichever comes first
Nothing — an over-length index is skipped
Only the topic files, because the index is ignored once it is long
questions.explanation: The index loads its first 200 lines or 25KB, and everything past the limit is dropped on the next load. Option 0 is tempting because CLAUDE.md loads in full up to 4 MiB — but MEMORY.md has its own, much smaller read limit.

questions.prompt: A teammate asks for your auto memory notes so they can get the same context. You copy `MEMORY.md` to their machine. What is the problem?
options: Nothing — auto memory is designed to be shared with the team
Auto memory is machine-local, and the useful detail lives in topic files that don't travel with the index
`MEMORY.md` is encrypted and cannot be copied
It works only if they also copy `~/.claude/settings.json`
questions.explanation: Auto memory is machine-local and the index only points at topic files, so a copied index references files the teammate doesn't have. Option 0 is tempting because sharing context is the goal — but the mechanism for sharing context across machines is a committed CLAUDE.md.

questions.prompt: You want the agent to stop taking its own notes in one repository, but keep the feature everywhere else. What do you set?
questions.explanation: Setting `autoMemoryEnabled` to false in one project's settings disables it there only. Option 0 is tempting because it disables auto memory — but it is an environment variable, so it applies to every project in that shell, not just one.
